The curved gold visor mirrors the colossal banded limb of an amber gas giant, its storm-bands smeared across the faceplate, the face behind lost in the glare.
A blazing white sun with knife-sharp diffraction spikes burns across the visor, the helmet rim haloed, the figure's silhouette a black shape behind the glare.
The visor reflects a planet's terminator line — a glittering arc of golden city-lights strung along the dark hemisphere, deep blue dayside curving above.
Amber HUD glyphs and a targeting reticle glow on the inside of the glass, overlaid on the swirling magenta nebula mirrored across the faceplate.
A swirling magenta-and-cyan nebula fills the curved visor, its gas tendrils distorted by the faceplate's dome, the astronaut's silhouette a dark ghost within.
The looming hull of the mothership curves across the visor, its running lights strung like embers, docking ports and scorched plating rendered in cold reflection.
Twin amber suns hang low on a planet's atmosphere curve, their doubled light bleeding across the visor in warm stacked halos, the horizon afire beneath.
A rippling green-and-violet aurora sheets across the faceplate, curtains of magnetized light smearing over the curved gold surface, the planet's dark limb below.
The astronaut's own gloved hand, reaching toward the viewer, fills the lower visor — small, distorted, urgent — the infinite black stretching behind the outstretched fingers.
A distant fleet of ships trails running lights across the visor like scattered embers, their hulls invisible, only the cold pinprick glow of dozens betraying them.
The moon's cratered grey face dominates the curved faceplate, every ancient impact scar rendered sharp, the terminator shadow cutting hard across its pocked surface.
An oncoming debris field blooms across the visor — tumbling hull fragments, frozen droplets, a shredded solar panel spinning end over end toward the lens.
A red dwarf's sullen crimson disk smolders low in the visor, its surface granulated with dark flares, the starfield around it dimmed to ember-orange haze.
The visor mirrors a volcanic moon, its surface split by lava rivers glowing amber-white, plumes of sulfur rising in slow arcs against absolute black.
A space station's rotating ring fills the curved glass, its windows strobing warm yellow, the docking arm extending toward the reflection's vanishing point.
A comet's bright nucleus blazes in the visor's upper arc, its blue ion tail streaming across the faceplate, the dust tail a soft amber smear beneath.
The visor reflects an approaching black hole's accretion disk — a tilted ring of white-hot plasma lensed into an impossible halo, spacetime bent around the rim.
A dense globular cluster blazes across the curved faceplate, ten thousand ancient suns compressed into a core bright as a second moon, edges fading to scatter.
The planet below fills the entire visor — cloud swirls, blue ocean, a continent's brown spine — the whole curved world distorted into the dome of one helmet.
Solar wind particles streak across the visor as faint aurora ribbons, threading between reflected stars, the sun a hard white point above the helmet's upper rim.
A crumbling asteroid tumbles in close reflection, its shadow falling across the faceplate, ancient regolith and exposed iron-bright metal catching the starbot's own suit lights.
The visor shows a deep-space rendezvous pod, thrusters firing white, closing distance fast — its running lights blinking in the curved gold mirror, face unknown behind the glow.
Ice-blue Cherenkov rings from a nearby reactor core shimmer across the faceplate, concentric and ethereal, the ship's dark spine visible behind them in cold silhouette.
A pulsar's precise lighthouse beam sweeps once across the visor — a white razor line cutting through nebula glow — gone in an instant, leaving afterburn on the gold.
The visor mirrors the crew's EVA tether line stretching into dark distance, a crewmate a tiny white figure at its far end, stars wheeling slowly behind them.
